rules.action: Enter on the first bar of the session where the condition holds
rules.condition: The selected contract has a valid bid and ask, and its spread is at most {long_max_spread:.0%} of mid for the long leg or {short_max_spread:.0%} for the short leg
rules.name: Entry trigger
rules.rationale:
There's no fixed entry time: liquidity decides when we trade, and fills are modeled at the mid.
If no bar in the session passes, the long waits for the next session, and the week's short is skipped by the no-quote gate.
rules.summary: On the first hourly bar where the contract has both a bid and an ask, and its spread is no wider than {long_max_spread:.0%} of mid for the long call or {short_max_spread:.0%} for the short call.
rules.title: When do we enter?

rules.action: Buy the long the expiry and strike rules select once the entry trigger passes. If it doesn't pass this session, retry each following session until it does
rules.condition: No long call is held: the window's first session, or a session in which a long reset or long roll sold it
rules.name: Long leg timing
rules.rationale: The long call is bought on the backtest's first day. This rule decides when; the expiry and strike rules decide which call.
rules.summary: Whenever we don't hold one: on the backtest's first session, or right after a long reset or long roll sold the last one. If no bar passes the entry trigger that session, we try again the next.
rules.title: When do we buy the long call?

rules.action: Keep every monthly expiry from {min_dte} to {max_dte} days to expiry; the strike rule chooses across them
rules.condition: Monthly expiries listed at the decision bar
rules.name: Long leg expiry
rules.rationale: The long can be any monthly in the range, so the strike rule looks for the cheapest replacement across all of them. Under Reg T a listed option with 9 months or less to expiry has no loan value; capping the range at {max_dte} days keeps the long always paid in full.
rules.summary: Any monthly expiry {min_dte} to {max_dte} days out; the strike rule picks the best contract across all of them.
rules.title: Which expiry do we use for the long call?

rules.action: Choose the lowest extrinsic ÷ delta, where extrinsic = mid − max(0, spot − strike). Ties go to the lower spread % of mid, then the earlier expiry, then the lower strike
rules.condition: Eligible calls with delta from {min_delta:.2f} to {max_delta:.2f} across the long leg's expiries
rules.name: Long leg strike
rules.rationale:
The long call is our stock substitute, and this is the cheapest way to buy that stock-like exposure: among the eligible calls, the one with the least extrinsic value per unit of delta.
Ties go to the tighter spread as a % of mid, then the earlier expiry, then the lower strike.
rules.summary: Among calls with delta {min_delta:.2f} to {max_delta:.2f}, the one with the lowest extrinsic value ÷ delta, where extrinsic = mid − max(0, spot − strike).
rules.title: Which long call do we buy?

rules.action: Buy a fixed quantity of {contracts}. No entry, logged, if it would make available funds negative. Every account starts with {cash_multiple}× the most expensive first long-leg cost in the universe, rounded up to the nearest ${cash_round_to:,.0f}
rules.condition: Every long entry
rules.name: Sizing
rules.rationale: One long call and one short call. Every symbol starts with the same cash, which is tracked for NAV and Reg T. An entry that would leave available funds negative isn't made; it's logged instead.
rules.summary: Buy {contracts} long call, but never if it would push available funds below zero. Each account starts with {cash_multiple}× the most expensive first long call in the universe, rounded up to the nearest ${cash_round_to:,.0f}.
rules.title: How large is the position?

rules.action: Sell a new short call; the entry trigger decides which bar
rules.condition: Each Monday (the first session of the week if Monday is a holiday), while a long call is held and no short is open
rules.name: Short leg timing
rules.rationale: One short call a week, sold as the week opens. If a short closes early, we wait for the next week instead of selling another straight away, so every new short has passed the skip-week gates.
rules.summary: On Monday, or the week's first session if Monday is a holiday, when we hold a long call, no short is open and no skip-week gate fires. The entry trigger decides which bar.
rules.title: When do we sell the weekly call?

rules.action: Use the expiry on that week's final trading session
rules.condition: Selling the week's short call
rules.name: Short leg expiry
rules.rationale: The short lives for one week. In a holiday week we never invent a Friday expiry: when the Friday is a holiday, it expires on Thursday.
rules.summary: The one expiring on the week's last trading session, which is normally Friday.
rules.title: Which expiry do we use for the short call?

rules.action: Choose the lowest listed strike ≥ spot + {k} × EM
rules.condition: Eligible calls on the short leg's expiry. EM is that week's at-the-money straddle mid: the ATM call mid + the ATM put mid
rules.name: Short leg strike
rules.rationale:
The expected-move short: it's sold at least {k} × the week's expected move above spot, the expected move being the at-the-money straddle's mid.
If that strike fails the entry trigger or the structural safety check, the week is skipped: we never substitute another strike.
rules.summary: The lowest listed strike at or above spot + {k} × the week's expected move, which is the ATM call mid + the ATM put mid.
rules.title: Which short strike do we sell?

rules.action: Sell as many contracts as the long leg holds
rules.condition: Selling the week's short call
rules.name: Short leg quantity
rules.rationale: Each short call is covered by a long call with a lower strike and a later expiry. That makes the position a diagonal spread, so the short needs no margin of its own under Reg T.
rules.summary: One for each long call we hold.
rules.title: How many short calls?

rules.action: Sell the short only if this holds; otherwise the structural-constraint gate skips the week
rules.condition: Short strike − long strike > long entry fill − short mid, per share
rules.name: Structural constraint
rules.rationale:
This keeps the gap between the strikes bigger than the net debit paid. Then, even if the short finishes deep in the money, the long's gain covers the short's loss plus the debit, so the position can't lose money overall.
It uses the long's entry fill, not its current mark, which keeps the check conservative.
rules.summary: Sell the short only if short strike − long strike > what we paid for the long − the short's mid, per share. If it doesn't hold, the week is skipped.
rules.title: Structural safety check

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Selected short never passes the entry trigger on any Monday bar
rules.name: No quote / liquidity
rules.rationale: No tradable quote, no trade: we never invent a fill or switch to another strike. A short whose spread is too wide is caught here too, since the entry trigger's spread threshold already rules it out, so no separate spread gate is needed.
rules.summary: The selected short call never passes the entry trigger on any Monday bar.
rules.title: No tradable quote

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Selected short fails the structural constraint
rules.name: Structural constraint
rules.rationale: A short that could turn the position into a net loss isn't sold, and we don't search for a replacement strike.
rules.summary: The selected short call fails the structural safety check.
rules.title: Structural constraint

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Front-week ATM IV ÷ next-week ATM IV > {max_ratio:.2f}
rules.name: Event week
rules.rationale: It's designed to catch weeks where the options market is pricing an unusual near-term event, usually earnings: an event priced into the front week lifts its implied volatility above the following week's. Reading that from the chain itself means no external earnings calendar is needed, and a ratio rather than a difference in vol points lets one threshold work for calm and volatile stocks alike.
rules.summary: Front-week ATM IV ÷ next-week ATM IV is above {max_ratio:.2f}.
rules.title: Event week

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Front-week ATM IV ÷ RV20 < {min_ratio:.2f}
rules.name: Volatility risk premium
rules.rationale: The volatility risk premium gate: we don't sell the weekly call when the front week's implied volatility is below the stock's realized volatility over the last 20 sessions (RV20).
rules.summary: Front-week ATM IV ÷ RV20 is below {min_ratio:.2f}.
rules.title: Volatility risk premium

rules.action: Skip the week; keep the long
rules.condition: Selected short mid < ${min_mid:.2f} per share
rules.name: Minimum premium
rules.rationale:
Below ${min_mid:.2f} a share there's too little premium to justify the trade, and we don't look for another strike.
In practice the entry trigger gets there first. Quotes are in whole cents, so below ${min_mid:.2f} a short's spread is wider than the entry trigger's 10% of mid unless its bid equals its ask. This gate therefore fires only on such a locked quote; otherwise the no-quote gate skips the week first.
rules.summary: The selected short call's mid is below ${min_mid:.2f} a share.
rules.title: Minimum premium

rules.action: Buy to close at mid. No new short until next Monday
rules.condition: Short mid ≤ {max_credit_fraction:.0%} of the credit received, on any bar before the Friday check
rules.name: Take profit
rules.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
Buy the short back once it has lost most of its value. This rule stops at the Friday check: from then on, that check and expiry decide.
rules.summary: If the short falls to {max_credit_fraction:.0%} or less of the premium we collected, on any bar before the Friday check, buy it back at mid. No new short until next week.
rules.title: Take profit

rules.action: Buy to close at mid. No new short until next Monday
rules.condition: Short delta > {max_delta:.2f}, on any bar
rules.name: Defensive
rules.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
It keeps the short from sitting deep in the money, where early exercise becomes likely and assignment risk grows.
rules.summary: If the short's delta rises above {max_delta:.2f}, on any bar, buy it back at mid. No new short until next week.
rules.title: Defensive exit

rules.action: Buy to close at mid
rules.condition: On the week's final session, at the last bar ending at or before {check_by:%H:%M} ET: spot ≥ short strike − {em_buffer:.2f} × EM, with EM measured at the short's entry
rules.name: Friday check
rules.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
The stock can move into the money in the final hour after the check. Treating anything within {em_buffer:.2f} × the expected move of the strike as in the money gets us out when the stock is close late on Friday, reducing missed assignments; the missed-assignment rule records any that still happen, rather than assuming them away.
rules.summary: On the week's last session, at the last bar ending by {check_by:%H:%M} ET, buy the short back at mid if spot ≥ strike − {em_buffer:.2f} × the expected move measured when it was sold.
rules.title: Friday risk check

rules.action: EXPIRE at $0
rules.condition: The short is still open at expiry and out of the money at the close (closing spot ≤ strike)
rules.name: Expires out of the money
rules.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
The call expires worthless, and we keep the full premium.
rules.summary: If the short is still open at expiry and the stock closes at or below the strike, it expires worthless.
rules.title: Short expires out of the money

rules.action: ASSIGN the call; open short stock at the strike (Reg T short-stock margin applies); buy to cover at the first valid bar of the next session
rules.condition: The short is still open at expiry and in the money at the close (closing spot > strike)
rules.name: Missed assignment
rules.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
Assignment only happens if the stock jumps past the strike after the Friday check, and the backtest records it honestly. While the short stock is open, Reg T short-stock margin applies.
Why we never let the short be exercised on purpose: buying back an in-the-money short at expiry costs its intrinsic value plus almost no extrinsic, which is economically equal to assignment and covering. Assignment only adds weekend gap risk on short stock, short-stock margin that can push available funds negative, or the loss of the long's extrinsic value if it's exercised to deliver.
rules.summary: If the short is still open at expiry and the stock closes above the strike, it's assigned: we're short the stock at the strike, and buy it back at the first valid bar of the next session.
rules.title: Missed assignment

rules.action: Sell long at mid, then re-enter by the long leg's entry rules in the same session if the entry trigger passes; then apply the short leg's entry rules
rules.condition: Long delta < {min_delta:.2f} at the Monday decision bar
rules.name: Long reset
rules.rationale: The long call is our stock substitute, and it's sold and re-bought if its delta falls below {min_delta:.2f}. Checking on Monday, before the week's short is sold, means a new short is always covered by the long we actually hold.
rules.summary: On Monday, if the long's delta is below {min_delta:.2f}, sell it at mid and buy a new one by the long entry rules that session, if the entry trigger passes. Then decide the week's short.
rules.title: Replace the long when its delta gets too low

rules.action: Same as the long reset
rules.condition: Long DTE < {min_dte} at the Monday decision bar
rules.name: Long roll
rules.rationale: Replacing the long before it's down to {min_dte} days keeps it acting like a long-dated stock substitute. Like the delta check, it's made on Monday, before the week's short is sold.
rules.summary: On Monday, if the long has fewer than {min_dte} days to expiry, replace it the same way as a long whose delta got too low.
rules.title: Replace the long when expiry gets close

rules.action: Mark all positions to the final bar's mid; no forced liquidation
rules.condition: The window's final bar
rules.name: End of backtest
rules.rationale: Open positions are valued at their last mid. Nothing is force-closed just because the backtest ends.
rules.summary: At the window's final bar, every open position is marked to its mid. Nothing is force-closed.
rules.title: End of the backtest

X-S4.summary: If the short is still open at expiry and the stock closes at or below the strike, it expires worthless.
X-S4.title: Short expires out of the money

X-S5.action: ASSIGN the call; open short stock at the strike (Reg T short-stock margin applies); buy to cover at the first valid bar of the next session
X-S5.condition: The short is still open at expiry and in the money at the close (closing spot > strike)
X-S5.rationale:
Why no rolls: with weekly shorts, next Monday's sale already is the roll. Rolling on the spot would let a new short skip the skip-week gates, and could turn a defined loss into an open-ended one.
Assignment only happens if the stock jumps past the strike after the Friday check, and the backtest records it honestly. While the short stock is open, Reg T short-stock margin applies.
Why we never let the short be exercised on purpose: buying back an in-the-money short at expiry costs its intrinsic value plus almost no extrinsic, which is economically equal to assignment and covering. Assignment only adds weekend gap risk on short stock, short-stock margin that can push available funds negative, or the loss of the long's extrinsic value if it's exercised to deliver.
X-S5.summary: If the short is still open at expiry and the stock closes above the strike, it's assigned: we're short the stock at the strike, and buy it back at the first valid bar of the next session.
X-S5.title: Missed assignment
